children: Kuala Lumpur Kepong's earnings are likely to be supported by favorable crude palm oil prices, driven by global biodiesel mandates and the delayed impact of El Nino on palm oil production, Affin Hwang IB analyst Nadia Aquidah says in a note. However, near-term prices are likely to remain under pressure from elevated Malaysian inventories, she says. Higher production costs and a lower CPO price assumption for 2028 prompts the analyst to cut the planter's FY2027-FY2028 earnings forecasts by 1.1% and 6.2%, respectively. Affin cuts KLK's target price to 22.00 ringgit from 22.60 ringgit, while maintaining a hold rating. Shares are 1.3% higher at 21.34 ringgit. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
